brief: Oil's vertical surge is reversing: a massive up candle gave back gains almost as sharply the next day, oil again overshot its 200-day moving average by a wide margin, and RSI is reversing from almost the same level as the prior reversal. Zoomed out, oil is a range-bound asset prone to huge swings, so the note reads this as another violent swing inside that range, not the start of a lasting breakout, and flags that oil volatility is showing far less stress than July's spot spike or the March shock. Politically: since oil spiked in August, the probability of Democrats regaining the Senate has risen from 41% to above 50%, and with Brent near $110/bbl and the midterms seven and a half weeks out, markets must weigh how long Republicans tolerate elevated prices. Trump said Tuesday oil would stay high until after the midterms then fall sharply, but the note argues the administration could still act sooner to ease pressure, especially with the 10-year yield nearing 5%, since a Democratic sweep of Congress would also be costly. Oil holding above $100 through the midterms is therefore far from certain.
